full_judgment: 2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule in short are that the plaintiff-petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 441 of 1966 in the court of Subordinate Judge Khulna for permanent injunction on the allegation that the land measuring more or less 1907 acres within P.S. Debhata and Kaliganj of the District of Khulna belonged to five Sarnaker brothers, defendant Nos. 3-7, who are ex-rent receivers. They formed a co-operative society in the name of Debishahar Agriculture & Fish Farming Co-operative "Society Ltd. on 20.12.55. These five Sarnaker brothers handed over possession of the land to the Society. Thereafter Saraker brothers filed an application for certificate on 20(4) of the State Acquisition and" Tenancy Act, 1950 for, cultivation of the excess Khas land belonging to them through the Co-operative Society. A certificate was granted but subsequently that certificate was withdrawn by the Board of Revenue. As against that the Sarnaker brothers filed a writ petition before the East Pakistan High Court being Writ Petition No. 168 of 1964 but that petition was rejected on 12.1.65. As against that they filed a Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal to the then Pakistan Supreme Court which was also dismissed on 19.5.66. Being defeated in obtaining requisite certificate the plaintiffs-Society filed the present suit for declaration and permanent injunction against the Government who were trying to posses the "excess land of the five Sarnaker brothers. In that suit the plaintiff filed an application for temporary injunction, that application was allowed and temporary injunction was granted on 15-6-66. It appears from record that thereafter an application was filed by some persons for adding them as parties in the suit. That application for addition of party was allowed. As against that order plaintiff filed an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the High Court of East Pakistan being Civil Revision Case No. 11/5 of 1966 but that revision was abated as per court's order dated 30.11.72 as per provision of P.O.69 of 1972. In the meantime defendant No.4 died on 29.11.72 but the plaintiff did not take any step for substitution of the heirs of Basanto, aforesaid defendant No.4 one of the brothers, as such the suit abated as against the heirs of Basanto the defendant No.4. It appears that one Narayan Chandra Sarkar, son of Basanto, filed an application for adding him as a party as sole heir of Basanto as Basanto executed a will in his favour.
